stem.en: This question is about a different market: the one in Fig. 9.8 of your textbook. Its demand curve DD' and supply curve SS' cross at point E. At a price below E, point C on the supply curve is far to the left of point F on the demand curve. If the price stays there, what could happen next in a free market?

text.en: The price falls further, because there is a surplus at this price.
Nothing happens, because C and F are at the same price.
Buyers who cannot get the good are ready to pay more, so the price rises towards E.
Sellers offer the amount at F straight away, at the same price.

explanation.en: Below E, buyers want more (F) than sellers offer (C): there is a shortage. In a free market the price rises. Buyers then want less and sellers offer more, until the market reaches E.

hints.en: Which point shows what buyers want, and which shows what sellers offer? Which is larger?
